title: A summand determinant is locally a matrix characteristic polynomial
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, n a finite index set, and T,P matrices with P*P=P and T*P=P*T. For D(T,P) defined in [def-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly], there exist a finite family f_i generating the unit ideal and, for each i, a natural number d_i and a d_i by d_i matrix U_i over A localized away from f_i, such that the coefficientwise localization of D(T,P) is the characteristic polynomial of U_i. No condition on the global leading coefficient is asserted.

source.place: Tag 09XI, lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, proof of (3) implies (1), splitting and characteristic-polynomial paragraphs; local matrix realization made explicit by R2

proof.text: Reindex by Fin (card n) and let p be the linear endomorphism represented by P. Idempotence makes its range a split summand: its subtype and the codomain restriction of p compose to identity. Thus its range is finite projective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] to this one image, obtaining a finite unit-ideal standard cover on which its localized module is finite free. No cover of the complementary image or pairwise refinement is needed.

For each member of the cover apply [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-endomorphism-image-base-change]. Its tensor-to-image equivalence, composed with Mathlib IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange.equiv, identifies the localized original image with the range of the entrywise localized projector. Transfer finite freeness across this equivalence. In a nonzero localization choose Module.finBasis of this range.

The basis coordinates of the projector range give rectangular matrices Q and R for its inclusion and projection, with QR=P and RQ=1. For C denoting entrywise constant polynomials, set Qc=C(Q), Rc=C(R). Rewrite the defining determinant in [def-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly] as det(1+((X-T-1)Qc)Rc). Mathlib Matrix.det_one_add_mul_comm makes this det(1+Rc((X-T-1)Qc)). Since Rc Qc=1 and Rc commutes with the rectangular scalar X, its matrix is X-C(RTQ); its determinant is (RTQ).charpoly. These equalities are the proved private idempotentCharpoly_retract helper. The formula works even without TP=PT.

Apply Mathlib Matrix.det_reindexAlgEquiv directly to the defining polynomial matrix to identify the determinant after reindexing by Fin (card n). Apply Mathlib RingHom.map_det directly to Polynomial.mapRingHom of the localization map; its preservation of addition, subtraction, identity, multiplication, and constant polynomials, together with Matrix.charmatrix_map, identifies the localized determinant with the determinant of the localized matrices. No separate mapping or reindexing theorem is declared. Take U_i=R_i T_i Q_i and d_i equal to the finite basis size. If a localization is the zero ring, take d_i=0 and U_i=0; all polynomials there are equal. Empty ambient index sets are covered by the same construction. The original cover already spans the unit ideal.

from.place: steps 1 and 2: finite standard cover and local characteristic-polynomial identification

lean.statement:
theorem exists_standardCover_idempotentCharpoly_eq_charpoly
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {n : Type v} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (T P : Matrix n n A) (hP : P * P = P) (hTP : T * P = P * T) :
    ∃ (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A), Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ i : Fin r, ∃ (d : ℕ) (U : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) (Localization.Away (f i))),
        (idempotentCharpoly T P).map (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (f i))) =
          U.charpoly
